newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH LOSE BUT STILL MAKE IT TO LEAGUE CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH LOSE BUT STILL MAKE IT TO LEAGUE CUP FINAL.

text.p: Middlesbrough qualified for the first major cup final in their 121-year history on Wednesday despite being beaten 1-0 at home by Stockport County in the second leg of their English League Cup semifinal.

But Middlesbrough, who are also through to the semifinals of the F.A. Cup, survived the defeat to beat Stockport 2-1 on aggregate and clinch a place in the final against Leicester City at Wembley on April 6.
The expensively-assembled premier league team, who are struggling to avoid relegation to the first division, lived on their nerves after falling behind to a fifth minute goal scored by Sean Connelly.

Middlesbrough's only other final this century was a winning appearance in the 1976 semi-official Anglo-Scottish Cup. Before that they had been winners of the now defunct F.A. Amateur Cup in 1895 and 1898.

Stockport, assembled at a fraction of the cost of Bryan Robson's side, looked dead and buried after losing the home leg 2-0 two weeks ago but they revitalised their hopes when Connelly burst through after a quickly-taken free-kick and lashed an unstoppable angled shot past Middlesbrough keeper Mark Schwarzer with only five minutes played.

Stockport had a number of chances to score but their evening ended in disappointment. They had youngster Tony Dinning sent off for an off-the-ball trip on Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli in the closing stages and were left to rue what might have been.
In the premier league, West Ham improved their hopes of surviving the drop with a last-minute winner from Paul Kitson giving them a 3-2 victory over Chelsea at Upton Park.

Ruud Gullit's team appeared to have done enough to secure a point when Mark Hughes equalised with three minutes to play but Kitson's second goal of the night gave the Hammers three vital points. Julian Dicks (55th-minute penalty) and Gianluca Vialli, who put Chelsea ahead after 26 minutes, were the other scorers.

Fellow strugglers Southampton drew 0-0 at Leeds, while relegation-threatened Sunderland who surprisngly beat Manchester United 2-1 on Saturday, lost by the same score at Sheffield Wednesday after leading through Kevin Ball. David Hirst and Dejan Stefanovic scored for the home side who kept alive their push for a place in next season's UEFA Cup.
